state: Northwind checkout platform runs eight independently deployable Python services on Kubernetes: StorefrontGateway, CartService, PricingService, InventoryService, OrderService, PaymentService, FraudScreen and NotifyService. Each pod runs two containers: a business container with domain logic and a co-located traffic agent injected at deploy time. Business code never dials peers directly; outbound localhost calls are intercepted by the pod-local agent, which applies mutual TLS, load balancing, timeouts, retries, circuit breaking and tracing. A central traffic controller distributes routing tables, certificates and policy to all agents and collects telemetry, so operators change routing or security without rebuilding services. OrderService calls PricingService through a PricingClient contract with get_quote(sku, qty). Product now needs optional behaviors around that contract: short-TTL result caching for flash sales, retry with jitter for transient faults, latency histograms, and audit logging. The active set varies by region and feature flag and is chosen at startup from config. PricingClient implementations are generated from IDL and sealed against inheritance, callers hold only the contract type, and creating one subclass per combination would yield sixteen variants plus future growth.

state: NorthStar Insurance runs PolicyAdmin, CustomerDirectory, BillingLedger and ClaimsHandling as independently deployable units owned by separate teams on Java, .NET and Python stacks. Each unit publishes a WSDL contract to a central registry and all cross-unit calls use SOAP over HTTP with XML payloads; the AgentPortal web front end orchestrates them and there is no shared database. To adjust coverage an agent flow is: AgentPortal calls PolicyAdmin.getPolicy and CustomerDirectory.getCustomer to render an edit form for policy P-4412, the agent reviews premiums, beneficiaries and endorsements for 15-30 minutes while taking customer calls, then AgentPortal calls PolicyAdmin.updatePolicy and BillingLedger.reprice. During storm season two agents in different branches routinely open the same policy at the same time. Last quarter three such overlaps caused the second submit to silently erase the first agent's endorsement changes, mispricing premiums. PolicyAdmin uses Oracle and cannot keep a row locked while the agent thinks without blocking ClaimsHandling payouts that read the same rows. Conflicts remain rare and re-entering the form is cheap compared to blocking thousands of reads.

Each unit publishes a WSDL contract and talks to the others only through SOAP over HTTPS with XML payloads validated against shared XSD; a central directory holds endpoint addresses so Java, C# and PHP callers can bind without custom adapters. The same column lists and conversions repeat across request handlers and batch jobs, and a rename in DEDUCTIBLE forces edits in six classes plus two jobs. The team wants domain logic unit-testable without Oracle, wants one place to adjust column lists and type rules, and wants to add new claim subtypes without copying boilerplate. CatalogAuthority is the system of record for venue layouts, price tiers and blackout dates, updated 2-3 times daily by ops. ArchiveLoader snapshots cell heaps to object storage nightly for recovery. state: MetroRide runs city surge pricing on a fleet of identical PricingCell replicas. Each cell bundles request-handling code with a RAM-resident partition of zone demand, driver supply and active trip state, kept authoritative in process and flushed asynchronously to Postgres for durability. Capacity is added by starting more cells and repartitioning zones; no central database sits on the hot path. Coordination uses two replicated associative memories, DemandPool and DispatchPool, where cells post and take entries by content matching rather than direct calls, plus a direct peer link between the FareEngine logic in one cell and the DispatchHandler logic in its neighbor for low-latency handoff of trip assignments. In development the pair runs on one host over Unix domain sockets with a custom binary layout; in staging and prod they run across hosts over TCP with TLS, and the roadmap calls for a shared-memory link on roadside units. Today each side hard-codes peer hostnames, socket setup, retries and byte packing, duplicating lookup and framing code. Moving a replica breaks addresses and business logic cannot be exercised without live sockets.

state: NorthStar Fulfillment runs 40 autonomous pick rovers in a warehouse. An edge server hosts Fleet Supervisor which assigns pick missions (aisle, shelf, tote id). Each rover runs a Rover Supervisor on its onboard computer that expands a mission into three side-by-side activities: Navigation Sequencer driving to the aisle, Scanner Sampler pre-warming the barcode camera, and Lift Sequencer preparing forks. Each sequencer in turn calls leaf drivers on microcontrollers: Motor Driver, Lidar Sampler, Gripper Driver, which run 50 Hz control loops and hold exclusive hardware and network leases. Results flow upward: leaf status to sequencers, sequencer summaries to Rover Supervisor, mission outcome to Fleet Supervisor for tote accounting. Constraints: an operator may abort a mission from the dashboard, a Safety Monitor may trip on lidar proximity, or a 30 s mission deadline may expire. On abort the whole nested drive-scan-lift tree must stop promptly, release the gripper safely, close leases, and report aborted distinct from failed, without force-killing threads mid-critical-section or leaving orphaned drive loops burning battery after the caller is gone. Forceful thread kill has previously bent forks and corrupted tote counts.

state: HarborSide fulfillment operates 40 AMRs. Fleet Dispatcher on the edge server assigns transport jobs over a redundant WiFi pub/sub bus. Aboard each vehicle a Unit Supervisor accepts one job and splits it into locomotion and manipulation activities for a Locomotion Manager and an Arm Manager, both ticked at 20 Hz in isolated RTOS partitions. Those managers emit setpoint streams to Wheel Servo Loops and Gripper Servo Loops at 1 kHz on motor firmware and can preempt an activity on obstacle, slip, or low-battery signals. Setpoints flow strictly downward; health and completion signals flow upward; only the servo loops drive hardware. Safety audit requires every motion request queued to the Locomotion Manager to carry a resolved map frame with localization fix, then a velocity and force envelope checked against load, then a live interlock token from the cell monitor, in that exact sequence. Today TraverseOrder is a plain data holder with defaulted fields and independent setters used by routing, tuning, and test tools. Engineers omit the token, swap frame and envelope order, or queue half-filled orders that fail inside the servo loop, far from the mistake. Reviews and runtime checks have not stopped recurrence, and the team wants misuse to be caught by the compiler before an order can reach the queue.

state: HarborSide fulfillment center runs 40 mobile manipulators. Each robot carries an onboard Jetson board hosting three simultaneous loops: a MissionSequencer that steps a pick job through approach, align, grasp, transport and deposit phases and can preempt or suspend the lower loops, a NavigationUnit that consumes lidar and wheel odometry at 20 Hz and outputs velocity commands, and a ManipulationUnit that runs grasp scoring and force-compliant arm motion at 100 Hz. A separate safety board hosts a SafetyGuardian that watches human-proximity lidar and cuts motion output within 50 ms, reporting suspend and resume events upward. A FleetSupervisor on the warehouse edge server assigns jobs, tracks battery and map versions, and pushes route updates over MQTT while robots report phase status and heartbeats upward at 2 Hz. For simulation the team must run identical onboard code against replay logs. Today NavigationUnit builds its own helpers inside its constructor in Python: self.store = LidarMapStore('/maps/site.db'), self.clock = SystemClock(), self.gateway = CanMotorGateway(0x1A). ManipulationUnit similarly builds GraspPlanner(), ForceSensorReader() and the same gateway address. Unit tests needing a fake map, a manual clock or a loopback motor bus must monkey-patch internals or edit the classes, and a reviewer cannot tell what a unit needs without reading its body. Adding a second map backend for the new building would touch every unit.
